prompt: Which value is the most reasonable estimate for the speed of a person walking at a comfortable, steady pace?

answer.explanation: Human walking speed is typically between 1.0 m/s and 1.5 m/s (roughly 4 to 5 km/h).

distractor_explanations: Incorrect. 0.12 m/s (12 cm/s) is an extremely slow crawl, taking nearly 10 seconds to cover one metre.
Correct. 1.2 m/s corresponds to covering about 1.2 metres in each second, characteristic of normal walking.
Incorrect. 12 m/s is faster than an Olympic sprinter running the 100 m dash.
Incorrect. 120 m/s (over 430 km/h) is high-speed train or aviation cruising speed.
hints: How many metres does a person step across in one second?
12 m/s is 100 m in 8.3 s (faster than Usain Bolt).
solution: A typical human walking pace covers roughly one to one-and-a-half paces per second, where each pace is about 0.8 m. This yields an average speed of approximately 1.2 m/s (around 4.3 km/h). 12 m/s is sprinting speed and 0.12 m/s is crawling speed. Option B is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Highlight standard kinematics benchmarks: walking ~ 1.2 m/s, cycling ~ 5-8 m/s, car on highway ~ 30 m/s.
Ask students to calculate 100 m transit time at each candidate speed.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored as an original item on human locomotion speed.
